terms.meaning: A plan for how you will use your money each month.
All the money you receive, such as allowance or salary.
A cost that stays the same each month, like rent.
A cost that changes each month, like food or fuel.
Savings kept only for surprises, like a broken phone or illness.
Money saved a little each month for a known future cost, like tuition.
Interest earned on both your savings and the interest already added.
The % a bank pays you on savings, or charges you on a loan.
Paying for something later in instalments. Late payments bring fees.
Vietnam's record of how you repay loans. A bad record makes future loans harder.
Buying something suddenly, without planning, because of emotion.
What you own minus what you owe.

faq.q: I only get 3 million VND a month. Can I still save?
faq.a: Yes. Start with 5-10% and increase it later. Saving is a habit, not an amount.
It's a starting point. If rent is high, try 60/20/20 and cut wants first.

faq.q: Where should I keep my emergency fund?
faq.a: In a separate savings account you don't use for daily spending, so you're not tempted.

faq.q: Is a credit card bad for students?
faq.a: Not always, but only use it if you can pay the full balance every month.

faq.q: How big should my first emergency fund be?
faq.a: A good first target for students is 3-5 million VND.
